10. Concepts as categories

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-08-harmonise.Rmd
book-08-harmonise.Rmd

What you will learn

Use translated concept answers, distinguish recodes from column renames, and harmonise two different site vocabularies.

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

Translation follows the value type

A concept-valued answer is a category, not a quantity to average. In language 2, the declared value column supplies that type. Your variable name does not need the suffix _concept_id.

education <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
class(education)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

The event selects the education question; the reducer reads its last coded answer. Selecting the question concept as the value would answer a different question.

categories <- omop_recipe(variables = list(education = education),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(categories, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(categories, out = c(people = "D_categories"), conns = conns))
#>         people 
#> "D_categories"

Translation is the default. The data values become labelled factors on the server.

ds.omop.table("D_categories", "education", conns = conns)
#> D_categories$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6

You see category names and released counts. The concept IDs used in the definition are vocabulary identifiers; they do not appear as numeric answers in this table.

Recode answers to yes and no

An explicit label map changes categories by concept identity. It does not search for text in each site’s database.

fever <- omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900002L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"),
  labels = c("900301" = "yes", "900302" = "no"))
class(fever)
#> [1] "omop_variable" "list"

Only the declared answer concepts receive those labels. A missing answer stays missing; absence of a record is not a clinical “no”.

answers <- omop_recipe(variables = list(fever = fever),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(answers, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(answers, out = c(people = "D_category_answers"), conns = conns))
#>               people 
#> "D_category_answers"
recode_table_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_category_answers$fever", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
knitr::kable(book_counts(recode_table_result))
Category Count
yes 6
no 6

Full aggregate response

recode_table_result
#> $output.list
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_row.props
#>                         study
#> D_category_answers$fever site
#>                      yes    1
#>                      no     1
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_col.props
#>                         study
#> D_category_answers$fever site
#>                      yes  0.5
#>                      no   0.5
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
#>                         study
#> D_category_answers$fever site
#>                      yes    6
#>                      no     6
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_proportions
#> D_category_answers$fever
#> yes  no 
#> 0.5 0.5 
#> 
#> $output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_category_answers$fever
#> yes  no 
#>   6   6 
#> 
#> 
#> $validity.message
#> [1] "Data in all studies were valid"

This real ds.table call excludes missing answers and shows the supplied labels. ds.omop.table() additionally retains the complete published category contract, including declared zero levels, and handles punctuation in labels.

Rename the column separately

A column name identifies the variable; a label names one of its categories. Name an explicit variable in the recipe list, without changing what its answers mean.

renamed <- omop_recipe(variables = list(schooling = education),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(renamed, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(renamed, out = c(people = "D_renamed_categories"), conns = conns))
#>                 people 
#> "D_renamed_categories"
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_renamed_categories", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "person_id" "schooling"

The list name supplies the scalar variable name. A concept label map would instead change values inside that column. The visit walkthrough uses a value-preserving mutate alias when adding a new name to an already assigned date column.

ds.omop.table("D_renamed_categories", "schooling", conns = conns)
#> D_renamed_categories$schooling
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6

The education categories and counts are unchanged. Next we address differences between sites, where even the vocabulary names can vary.

Rename automatically generated concept columns

Some layouts expand one event into separate columns for each concept. A panel of inpatient/outpatient counts is one example. column_names targets their stable generated keys, not the explicit scalar variable from the previous step.

visit_event <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", c(9201L, 9202L), name = "visits")
visit_population <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visit_event))
renamed_panel <- omop_recipe(events = list(visit_event),
  populations = list(visit_population),
  column_names = c(visits_9201_count = "admissions", visits_9202_count = "outpatient"),
  outputs = omop_output("panel", rows = "visitors", format = "person_period",
    options = list(sources = list(visit_event), bins = list(width = 30L),
      window = omop_window(0, 29), analyses = "count")))
recipe_explain(renamed_panel)$selected
#> [1] "v2"

The keys combine the source name, concept identity and analysis. They remain stable when a vocabulary changes its wording; your chosen column names remain readable. An explicit name cannot collide with a protected or another final column.

stopifnot(recipe_explain(renamed_panel, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(renamed_panel, out = c(panel = "D_renamed_panel"), conns = conns))
#>             panel 
#> "D_renamed_panel"
dsBaseClient::ds.colnames("D_renamed_panel", datasources = conns)
#> $site
#> [1] "row_id"            "cohort_row_id"     "person_id"         "period_start_days"
#> [5] "period_end_days"   "days"              "admissions"        "outpatient"

The resulting count columns have your declared names. Using column_names with an explicit scalar name such as education would not rename that scalar column.

Open two practice connections

The other lessons use one server. This check uses two DSLite connections. Both synthetic databases hold the same answer IDs. The second vocabulary calls University education “University qualification” and declares a newer vocabulary version. No patient records are downloaded.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
pair <- book_fixture(two_sites = TRUE)
two_conns <- pair$conns
names(two_conns)
#> [1] "site"  "site2"

Each name represents a separate DataSHIELD session with its own private table.

See the vocabulary difference 

lookup <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(900102L, conns = two_conns)
lapply(lookup$per_site, function(x) x["concept_name"])
#> $site
#>           concept_name
#> 1 University education
#> 
#> $site2
#>               concept_name
#> 1 University qualification

This is permitted vocabulary metadata, not observed answer frequencies.

Declare a shared label 

harmonised <- omop_recipe(variables = list(education = omop_variable(
  event = omop_event("observation", concepts = 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"),
  labels = c("900102" = "University education"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
stopifnot(recipe_explain(harmonised, conns = two_conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(harmonised, out = c(people = "D_shared"), conns = two_conns))
#>     people 
#> "D_shared"

A common explicit label resolves the known wording difference. Harmonisation is based on concept identity and the published label contract, not on matching patient records or guessing that similar words mean the same thing.

Compare released category sets 

site_tables <- lapply(names(two_conns), function(site)
  ds.omop.table("D_shared", "education", conns = two_conns[site]))
names(site_tables) <- names(two_conns)
site_tables
#> $site
#> D_shared$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6 
#> 
#> $site2
#> D_shared$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                    6                    6
identical(dimnames(site_tables[[1]]), dimnames(site_tables[[2]]))
#> [1] TRUE

Both real executions returned the same category set. Now combine their counts:

ds.omop.table("D_shared", "education", conns = two_conns)
#> D_shared$education
#>  Secondary education University education 
#>                   12                   12

The pooled counts add released cells. They do not link people across sites. In a real network, confirm the concept meanings as well as their labels.

Recap

Concept values translate by default. Label maps recode answers; column maps rename variables. Shared labels give common categories across vocabulary wording differences, after you confirm concept meanings.

Try it

Check the selected recipe language once more, then close both temporary connections.

Solution

recipe_explain(harmonised, conns = two_conns)$selected
#> [1] "v2"
ds.omop.disconnect(conns = two_conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(two_conns)
unlink(pair$path)
